posts.title: The Autumnal dilemma
posts.description: Every year I look forward to a walk in the woods. To hear the rustle of fallen leaves beneath my feet. To enjoy the beauty of all the colours, particularly when there is some welcome sunlight piercing through the surrounding golden canopy. I defy anyone not to be entranced by simply being in a deciduous woodland at this time of year. However it presents me with a dilemma. From a photographic standpoint I feel I should retain all the colours and forget for once that I am a black and white photographer. I am therefore torn, pulled in one direction only to be pushed back in another. The result is often that I return from an outing with my camera with nothing of note. I find colour work challenging. I am outside my comfort zone but those colours are just so pleasing to the eye aren’t they? This year though I stuck to my guns having learnt from past experience. posts.title: Where have I been…..…???
posts.description: There are three answers to this one question. All three have relevance and I’ll start with the most obvious response, which relates directly to the images in this entry. Many of you may recognise the subject of the above image. Yes, I have been to Corfe Castle in Dorset. I have to say that I normally try and steer clear of a honeypot location such as this. The very mention of this iconic place and the mind immediately conjures up a picture of the castle ruins rising out of early morning mist, bathed in warm dawn light. It’s a beautiful sight but it’s something of a cliche in the photographic world. Metaphorically speaking, tripod holes are all too evident! If at all possible I prefer to approach a well known subject with a different eye and avoid making similar images to those that have ventured there before me. posts.title: Is it a Holga or a Hasselblad? ….. no it’s a Bronica
posts.description: Zenza Bronica SQ-Ai In my last post – ‘Should I buy a Holga or a Hasselblad?’ – I explored the idea of getting a medium format camera to kick start my journey into the analogue world of 120 film. I have been a serious hobbyist for 15 years, so it’s taken me a long time to come round to the idea of shooting film. Following the publication of this post I received a comment from Chris Rusbridge for which I am most grateful. He suggested I should consider a Bronica SQ. I had heard of the Bronica but knew very little about it so I started searching for information. The more I discovered the more this camera appealed to me. Truth be told but I spend far too much time reading reviews and watching YouTube videos. I dither, then dither some more. But for me it’s part of the fun before deciding on a new piece of camera gear. Based on my initial findings I quickly dismissed the Holga.
